name: starting architecture
last_analysis: All 9 trials scored exactly 0 on both seeds, and training success was also 0. That held across recipes (1, 2 and 4 epochs; lr, entropy and gamma changes) and across heads (footprint pooling, layer-resolved, footprint-concat, dense, transformer). A policy that is merely weak should still build a few 6-brick designs exactly. A flat 0 instead suggests a structural mismatch: this world probably decodes actions differently from the stated layout. It might transpose or flip y and x, order actions cell-first instead of type-first, or put DONE first. Local convolutional heads cannot learn such a remapping. The dense and positional-transformer heads could learn it in principle, but probably too slowly with about 250k samples. So in this last round, every candidate scores several possible action layouts at once and sums them. Each layout gets its own small learned output map, so training can strengthen the correct one and shrink the others toward zero.
